sections.title: Property damage restoration in Poetry: use a small investigation to resolve a larger choice
paragraphs: A stained cabinet side might need cleaning, a replacement panel or removal to reach the wall. We will inspect its construction and explain any authorized opening or treatment trial before recommending the larger scope. The result should identify the affected layer, rather than simply produce a larger demolition allowance.

sections.title: Compare what each recovery option includes
paragraphs: Retaining a component can require detachment, cleaning on concealed faces and drying before refitting. Replacement can require utility disconnection or changes at an adjoining finish. We will include those physical connections when comparing the options so a low initial price does not omit necessary work.

sections.title: Make the next commitment from the exposed condition
paragraphs: Removed material may reveal another wet or contaminated surface. We will explain the treatment needed there and identify which earlier assumptions have changed. Agreed cleanup and applicable evaluation come before ordering finishes that would conceal the finding.

water-damage-restoration/poetry.intro: Water damage restoration in Poetry can be needed after water enters around a window and dampens the sill, casing or wall below. sections.title: Water damage restoration in Poetry traces the window edge
paragraphs: We will inspect the sill, lower corners and adjoining wall finish for swelling or separation, then check accessible material for moisture. If trim blocks the path, careful removal can expose the joint and show whether the wall backing or insulation also needs attention.
Interior drying does not correct water entry at the exterior opening. The source repair should be identified separately, with the affected interior materials checked after it is complete.

sections.title: Dry or remove the layers behind the trim
paragraphs: Sound materials that can be reached may be dried with follow-up checks. Swollen trim, softened backing or material that cannot be adequately dried may need removal. We will explain that choice based on the exposed condition instead of the stain size alone.

sections.title: Replace the edge after the opening is ready
paragraphs: The repair scope can specify new casing or sill material, a prepared wall edge and the agreed paint boundary. If access uncovers a separate mold concern, the responsible provider and work scope are disclosed before that remediation begins.

sections.title: Mold remediation in Poetry: inspect the concealed contact faces
paragraphs: The back of a wardrobe may be unfinished fiberboard even when its doors have a washable finish. We will identify that construction and the affected wall material separately. Moving the unit will be planned within the work controls so it does not carry loose affected material into the receiving space.

sections.title: Treat the exposed wall and evaluate the furniture backing
paragraphs: Specified affected wallboard or insulation will be removed and packaged. Suitable retained framing receives controlled particle collection and detailed cleaning, including the connection previously covered by the wardrobe. A deteriorated absorbent furniture back may require replacement or disposal rather than the process used on an intact coated side.

sections.title: Choose where the belongings can return
paragraphs: Cleaned property will remain separate from unresolved items. Moisture correction and any required completion review must establish the receiving wall condition before the wardrobe conceals it again. We will explain unfinished furniture interiors rather than describe a clean exterior as a complete recovery.

sections.title: Fire and smoke damage restoration in Poetry: check the finish before brushing or washing
paragraphs: Raised texture and recessed joints can hold soot after a flat area looks clean. A controlled treatment trial will establish whether suitable particle collection and compatible cleaning can reach those details without unacceptable finish loss. An unstable or flaking coating needs a different decision from removable residue.

sections.title: Reach the detail without enlarging finish damage
paragraphs: We will collect loose deposits and clean accepted surfaces with tools and methods suited to their profile. Adjacent trim and accessible ledges will be included where contacted. Loose plaster, failed attachment or other damage exposed during this work will be identified for appropriate repair rather than scrubbed repeatedly.

sections.title: Decide whether the recovered surface needs decoration
paragraphs: Residual discoloration and remaining removable deposits are different findings. We will explain the cleaned condition before the owner chooses refinishing, keeping plaster repair and decorative matching separate from the soot-cleanup result. Affected furnishings still require their own recovery assessment.

sections.title: Clean both sides of a moved object’s footprint
paragraphs: The underside of a suitable hard container and the floor beneath it are separate surfaces. We will physically remove soil from retained surfaces before appropriate disinfection, following the selected product requirements. Objects still awaiting a recovery decision will be kept out of completed areas.

sections.title: Reopen concealed edges where the release reached them
paragraphs: A wet threshold or lower trim joint may require authorized removal to reach the contacted base. After treatment, retained components will be checked for drying needs. The source repair and any missing finish remain explicit before clean belongings return.

sections.title: Install without trapping a moving floor
paragraphs: Once the base and prior restoration work are ready, the selected flooring will be fitted using its installation requirements. Where a system needs movement clearance, perimeter trim will finish the edge without pinning the moving surface. Threshold attachment will suit the particular assembly rather than rely on one fastening method for every product.

sections.title: Check the completed connection in use
paragraphs: We will check door movement and the fitted transition, then reset included base or shoe trim. Any adjustment beyond the agreed floor scope will be identified before work expands. Matching an older adjoining finish remains a selection decision, distinct from making the connection function properly.

checklist: Identify the replacement floor and underlayment if selected.

Share which adjacent floors and trim will remain.
